notes.title: CONTENT UPDATE & USER REVIEWS TRAILER
notes.content:
We have been overwhelmed by the love and support you have given us since we released Clash: Artifacts of Chaos. A simple thanks did not seem nearly enough, so we prepared several surprises for you to enjoy!

[h3]NEW GAME PLUS[/h3]

You asked for it, here it is: the New Game Plus mode. Once the game is finished, you will be able to start again with the upgrades you already got and face tougher, higher-level opponents. This mode also includes exclusive content: a new war paint for Pseudo, new hats for the Boy and a new set of armor for Pseudo to be found in-game. Will you take on the challenge? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/9be5d4d63c54a38a89354136a4cb8554aaeb40f8.png[/img]

[h3]FIXES AND IMPROVEMENTS [/h3]

This new update incorporates various fixes and improvements to the gameplay experience:

• [i]Quality of life[/i] - At night, the location of Dark Bosses (optional end-game challenges) is displayed on the world map 
• [i]Quality of life[/i] - Next objectives displayed after beating the Director, as some players told us they were getting lost at this stage
• [i]Options[/i] - On first launch, the game now asks the player to set the main parameters: animated or static textures, world loading by streaming or by zones.
• [i]Cinematics[/i] - New Boy kidnapping cinematics
• [i]New technology[/i]: the advanced NVIDIA Ansel screen capture tool
• Various bug fixes
 
[h3]A TRAILER TO THANK ALL OF YOU [/h3]

A 95% Steam user score is no small feat and we are deeply grateful to all players that took the time to write a review of Clash. We hope you enjoy this trailer made in fashion of a traditional Accolades Trailer, but with players reviews instead!  

[previewyoutube=WwcAxxb6D5U;full]https://youtu.be/WwcAxxb6D5U[/previewyoutube]

Our special thanks to Ross, SgtLemon1, Throkgaar, Moffein, Dread Guacamole, Eternal Optimist, Magnus, Fox with a cap, ImperialPanda and cronkin tompler who were kind enough to agree on having their review featured in the trailer. We would also like to thank Nogueh, Cahalit, strenkth, and all others that agreed to participate but that we could not integrate in the end: your reviews were a joy to read and we are thankful from the bottom of our heart. 

Our thanks too to all the players of Clash for taking on this incredible journey with Pseudo and the Boy across Zenozoik. We hope you had as much as a blast than us! 

Feel free to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/theACETeam]Twitter[/url],  join our [url=https://discord.gg/dcGxnjt]Discord[/url] or go in the Steam discussions board if you’d like to keep up with all future news and share your thoughts with us – we would love to hear them. 

[i]-  The Clash: Artifacts of Chaos Team[/i]

notes.title: Looking for Feedback — Navigation & Getting Lost
notes.content:
When designing Clash we knew from the get go that choosing not to implement waypoints, guided instructions, fast travel... (and asking people to actually explore the world on foot to figure out where to go) was a challenging proposition. The norm in game development (for years) has been about telling players where to go and when.

We made the best efforts to make our world as intuitive as possible without spoiling it all with a guided mechanic that holds your hand.

However, we understand that getting lost for hours isn't fun, so we'd like to ask players who have beaten the game (or played it a lot) to share which locations they felt were hard to navigate through or find. We're compiling info and will add some assets in our level design to help lead people in the right direction in upcoming game updates. Rest assured, we'll only move around decorations or add a few colourful assets, or signs, and won't introduce a "guided" exploration mechanic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/1bbffb5ad397c71c2358e2ace03448c2540ceecf.jpg[/img]

Screenshots / descriptions / anything... we appreciate any info that can be used to help make the game better for everyone, while remaining true to its vision. ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos review
notes.content:
Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is like the anti-God of War. It bears a family resemblance to Sony’s franchise revival, enough to invite comparison, but its design philosophy could hardly be more different. In particular, if you ever thought God of War would benefit from a more hands-off approach to nudging you through its adventures, then rest assured Clash keeps its sweaty palms strictly to itself.

If that sounds heavenly for those who prefer their games not to be littered with symbols and NPC chatter telling them where to go and how to get there, however, beware the old adage: "Be careful what you wish for, you might just get it." Pushing through Clash’s lush world and sprinkled narrative is often a richer experience due to the absence of supervisory noise. Yet it swings the pendulum of player guidance so far to the opposite extreme you may find yourself crying out for a quest marker or eager companion to show the way... Read more.

notes.title: DEV BLOG: How we Gave Clash its Unique Art Style
notes.content:
[h3]Hello everyone, and welcome to this dev blog about a topic we often get asked about: our game’s stylized rendering! 
[/h3]
Video games can use many different styles to create a unique look and feel. For Clash, we knew from the beginning that we wanted to use a very colorful and non-realistic one for many reasons: to set it apart from other games in the genre, to allow us to stylize and exaggerate the animation and color palette, and to approximate the illustrations and punk-fantasy art that inspired the creation of the world in the first place.

[b]Stylized rendering is a powerful tool[/b] that highlights that “[i]What to draw?[/i]” and “[i]How to draw it?[/i]” are two different questions. This is the third time we have visited the surreal world of Zenozoik and its primitive humanoid animal inhabitants, but it is the first time we are approaching the “[i]how to draw it[/i]” with a really different technique!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/f63d9dc1f37a164e6df787112156c1bc74f774df.gif[/img]

There are many ways we could have gone, and we tested several different styles before landing on the one we used. By choosing what to simplify and what to exaggerate, you get very different effects. One of the more interesting styles we tested was a painterly thick brushstroke look.

It allowed [b]very expressive shapes, a messy almost impressionistic look[/b], and was certainly very different. We eventually decided against this style because of the excessive simplification it produced: our artists always wanted to add more small details to characters and environments, details which would not really shine in this impressionistic style.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/657588742fe1702da8f1d6e1efb2d135ea70e666.jpg[/img]

The [b]rendering style we ended up going for is called hatching, or crosshatching[/b]. It is a drawing style that creates shading and conveys lighting by drawing closely spaced lines. The closer the lines are together, the darker the area will appear. This style is often used in traditional drawings, illustrations, and comic books, and gives the artwork a hand-drawn look. This technique allowed us to achieve an illustrated style while still preserving detail.

By [b]separating the lighting information and conveying light intensity and detail mostly with the ink pencil linework, we can treat color as a separate layer[/b]. This allows us to use more artificial color schemes which would look strange in a realistic rendering style but feel consistent with the look of an illustration. Violet and orange skies, characters with blue or yellow skin, orange dirt, cyan and green mineral deposits in the mountain walls… we intentionally use saturated colors, or color combinations 
hard to find in nature to convey this is a different world.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/8767200d314dbaec1c83b0c81691701aeaf724cb.jpg[/img]

One of the main challenges to make the hatching style work was to make sure that it worked at different distances and different levels of detail. It is not just drawing lines on the surfaces, because what works for small details up close might not work for a mountain at a distance.

Also some features must be preserved more carefully, like character eyes which are a focus point and must always remain well defined and sharp. The linework needs to be consistent to seem like it was all done with the same tool.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/54c8bac296af3ff93f6388adb8f25ee6d234a626.jpg[/img]

Finally, while we have designed a very specific look for the game, we still chose to enable configuration options for players to personalize the look. [b]Players can choose a cleaner look or add and remove effects[/b]. We even left in a comic book inspired black and white mode, which is not ideal for readability, but is still very cool to play with!

Less than one month are left until the launch and we look forward to all of you playing and exploring the world we created. If you wish to follow other news and future dev blogs, don’t hesitate to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/theACETeam]Twitter[/url] or join our official [url=https://discord.gg/dcGxnjt]Discord[/url] server.  And as always, feel free to let us know what you think in the Steam discussions board, we can’t wait to hear it!  

[b][i]- Edmundo Bordeu, Art Director at ACE Team[/i][/b]

notes.title: Warthog fistfights, barrel goblins, and wooden ghosts: This action-RPG is 10 times weirder than Elden Ring
notes.content: Every enemy in Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is like its own bizarre work of art. From an antelope with horns for legs, to a grotesque, frying pan-wielding barrel goblin, to a silent warrior in some kind of symbiotic relationship with a crab, every single one is so creative and lurid that you just want to walk up, stare at them and drink in all the weird details. But I can tell you from experience that if you do that, they'll smash your face in until you turn into a ghost made of wood. Er, more on that later... Read more.

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Demo - Patch Notes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/9c5128fcce7c11e9a639f0e52666f29af3992326.png[/img]

Howdy All, 

Thanks for checking out the Clash: Artifacts of Chaos demo as part of the Steam Next Fest. We've been blown away by the support and feedback we've received so far. We're hard at work preparing for the release on February 9th, but we couldn't leave some of the problems with the demo unaddressed.

So we've pushed out a small patch that should fix a few cases of crashing and expand on a few missing options. As always, we remain disposable on our [url=https://discord.gg/DrDtKwtb2r]Discord[/url] and in the Steam Discussion boards if you have any more feedback. 

[h3]Steam Fest Demo Patch[/h3][list][*] Added Invert Y axis to camera options in settings menu.
[*] Added camera sensitivity options in the settings menu.
[*] Fixed crash in dialog manager.
[*] Fixed crash related to challenge totems.
[*] Fixed stability issue related to achievements.
[*] Fixed AIs not locating the player if they were too far away.
[*] Ensured enemies will not retreat when they are engaged in first person.
[*] AIs not participating in the Ritual can no longer attack the player during it.
[*] Manual camera lock is enabled on ragdolled enemies.
[*] Area confinement function uses a collision mesh instead of gradually affecting the player’s velocity.[/list]

notes.title: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos - Steam Fest Demo FAQ
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/5cfb0f3e8a1c27d0544832b3a8c8bc55336fc047.png[/img]

Welcome to Steam Next Fest where you'll have the opportunity to try a demo of Clash: Artifacts of Chaos. Experience the opening moments of the game where you'll take on the mantle of Psuedo, a hermit who lives on the outskirts of a chaotic society that only obeys one law, the Ritual.

Get your own taste of Clash: Artifacts of Chaos now by playing the demo during Steam Next Fest and don't forget to wishlist in preparation for launch on February 9th, 2023 and if you want to know more, read the FAQ below:

[h2]Clash: Artifacts of Chaos - Steam Next Fest demo FAQ[/h2]

[h3]In which languages is the demo available?[/h3]
English, French, German, Polish, Italian, Spanish (Spain), Spanish (Latam), Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional)

[h3]Which devices are supported? Can inputs be rebinded?[/h3]
You can play with either a mouse and keyboard or a controller. Visit Settings > Controls to rebind keyboard inputs and/or switch between the four controller presets.

[h3]What are the minimum and recommended specs?[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/1927ae4905bc893eab82dc77b66d5883f2d4aa74.png[/img]

[h3]How long is the demo? [/h3]
Experiencing all the content of the demo takes around three to five hours.

[h3]Is multiplayer supported?[/h3]
Not in this demo, but it will be in the full release.

[h3]How can I save my progress?[/h3]
Progress is automatically saved whenever you visit one of your camps. Remember to set up camp when you discover an empty fireplace.

[h3]How can I brew health potions?[/h3]
Pick up ingredients in the wild, such as honey or frogs, and interact with the cooking pot at your campfire. Different combinations of ingredients will brew different potions.

[h3]How can I unlock and equip new special attacks and stances?[/h3]
You may find stone totems when exploring. Interacting with them will trigger a fight. If you're victorious, you'll gain a new special attack or a new combat stance. You can change your equipped special attacks and stance by interacting with the training dummy at your camps.

[h3]Are there armors and weapons in this game?[/h3]
Weapons and armor pieces can be found by exploring the world or acquired from shopkeepers at a village. Shopkeepers will require specific components which can be found by exploring and fighting animals. Armor pieces provide passive bonuses to your attributes. Weapons allow new attacks until they break down from overuse.

[h3]Does the demo include Steam achievements or Steam trading cards?[/h3]
Five achievements can be unlocked by playing the demo. Trading cards can’t be collected from free demos.

[h3]I have more questions![/h3]
We have more answers! Read the FAQ of the full game: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1430680/discussions/0/3038228110739530355/

Last night we revealed the first look at Clash: Artifacts of Chaos during the ID@Xbox event. Welcome back to the world of Zenozoik, but unlike how you've ever seen it before. In this 3rd person action-brawler you play as Pseudo, a hermit living out his reclusive lifestyle on the fringes of a weird and wonderfully chaotic society. 

This society has one law, the Ritual, a game that can influence the rules of combat. Pseudo finds himself drawn back into this world when he comes across the Boy, a small helpless creature he decides to protect. This simple action triggers a story that will see the pair trailed by mercenaries as they travel the world and go up against Gemini, the fabled mistress of the Artifacts. 

Check out the video and don't forget to follow us on socials [url=https://twitter.com/ClashAOC]@ClashAoC [/url] or let us know what you think on the Steam Community Hub.

Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is scheduled for release in November 2022!

notes.title: Level Design in Clash: Artifacts of Chaos
notes.content:
The first Zeno Clash and its sequel both had very different approaches for their level design. They both had the common goal of showing players a rich world with very distinct and unique locations - but they both approached that goal from a different angle:

Zeno Clash 1 was made by such a small team that we had to create the illusion of scale by having small combat areas surrounded by larger portions of the world you could see in the horizon, yet never visit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/bccad3f06a93376d1be5b51179e9cc315cf0a843.jpg[/img]
[i]Zeno Clash (2009)[/i]
[hr][/hr]

Zeno Clash 2, with its bigger scope allowed players to explore through large interconnected levels, and was much larger, yet the open ended levels offered more space than we were actually capable of filling - making exploration less exciting than we could have hoped for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/e25786607b475ce2d88f3997b287eda3c168774c.jpg[/img]
[i]Zeno Clash 2 (2013)[/i]
[hr][/hr]

Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is neither “A” nor “B”. It is “C”. And it is much better than our previous attempts. It is also a reason why the Souls games have a strong influence in the design of this game. I once saw a video of famous youtuber “Maximilian Dood” where he ranked Souls-Like games from worst to best, which ended up with Bloodborne taking the #1 spot. Maximilian, despite focusing primarily on fighting games (and combat mechanics), said that it was probably the world design what gave Bloodborne the crown, and I wholly agree. Bloodborne is a masterpiece of level design - and From Software games are excellent in this regard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/ce7ac77ce98b517b89da9ecd4d1cf959874319ad.jpg[/img]
[i]An editor view of the level design of Clash suggests a much more interesting "maze-like" layout with multiple paths and interconnecting areas[/i]
[hr][/hr]

Clash has a fully interconnected world that is inspired by Bloodborne (but is not entirely the same). Our game has no actual discernible levels. It has one large world that never goes into a loading screen. “Maps” (or areas of different themes) are interconnected in surprising ways, and discovering / enabling shortcuts is an essential part of the design. You can also see areas of the game at a distance which you cannot access until later portions of the adventure.

The design is not restricted to small combat arenas, and is not based on large open areas that lead to others. We are doing intricate level design - something certainly new for the series. Maps are not too large or small - they are the size they need to be based on what we expect the player to be doing at the moment. And by itself this leads to a surprising enjoyment of traversing and discovering the world. Just getting from one area to another is fun - regardless of the combat or content of such levels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/fb4586bdd0a1abbfd26b903595c1c7a0414bae48.jpg[/img]
[i]Clash: Artifacts of Chaos[/i]
[hr][/hr]

The world and level design has been one of my main areas of responsibility for this project. When we started working on the environments the directive for the team was: “We have a mission - and that is no matter how other parts of the game end up, level design has to be interesting enough to almost carry the game experience through by itself. It has to be one of the brightest aspects of the experience. We are not making a canvas for other game mechanics to exist… the level design must be a game of its own.”

We look forward to seeing people explore our game world next year, and are excited to share more about other exciting features in development. Stay tuned for more information as we continue development of Clash: Artifacts of Chaos.

If you wish to follow other news, follow us on Twitter https://twitter.com/ClashAoC ...and don't forget to follow us and wishlist on Steam ːsteamhappyː

Carlos Bordeu

notes.title: Return to the world of Zenozoik in Clash: Artifacts of Chaos!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40847511/e92b4700b459168442dd2f8fc8f71f2f55441366.png[/img]

Hello Everyone,

Were you surprised by our new announcement? We hope you're ready to return to the world of Zenozoik in our new game, Clash: Artifacts of Chaos. 

In Clash: Artifacts of Chaos, you play as Pseudo, a powerful warrior on a quest to obtain the Artifacts of Chaos. We don't want to dive too deep into the story just yet, but fans of Zeno Clash will be happy to know there are ties to the other games. Though equally, the game is designed as a stand-alone experience, and it's not necessary to have played those titles to enjoy Clash: Artifacts of Chaos. 

We'll be sharing more about the game throughout development, so keep your eyes open here and on our [url=https://www.facebook.com/ClashAoC]Facebook[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/ClashAOC]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.gg/dcGxnjt]Discord[/url] for all the updates!
